title: Agent and server: device-code pairing
description: Pairing an agent with an operator (spec: Identity and access > Agents), modelled on the OAuth device authorization grant (RFC 8628), over versioned HTTPS. POST /api/v1/agent/pairing takes pairing_request and answers pairing_code. POST /api/v1/agent/pairing/token takes pairing_poll and answers pairing_status or, once, pairing_token. The token then goes into Authorization: Bearer on every request and websocket subscription. Accepted 2026-10-26 (spec-feedback item 16).

pairingId.description: Secret that identifies the pairing between agent and server. Never shown to the operator.

pairingCode.description: Server to agent: the code the agent shows to its operator.

userCode.description: Shown by the agent; the operator types it in on the verification page. No 0, O, 1 or I.

verificationUrl.description: The page where the signed-in operator enters the code, for example https://<host>/pair.

expiresAt.description: After this the code no longer works (10 minutes).

pairingPoll.description: Agent to server: has the operator approved?

pairingStatus.description: Server to agent: not (yet) approved. pending: poll again after intervalSec. slow_down: polled too early, wait intervalSec. denied and expired are final: start again. An unknown pairingId is answered with expired.

pairingToken.description: Server to agent, once, after approval. The server stores only a hash of the token; the operator can revoke it. The agent uses this agentId in all its messages.
